title: Superpolynomial arithmetic formula lower bounds
formal:
Is the permanent family outside polynomial-size arithmetic formulas over \(\mathbb C\)? Precisely, is the following assertion true?
\[
\forall K,C\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \exists n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\
\forall F,\qquad
\llbracket F\rrbracket=\operatorname{Perm}_n
\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{size}(F)>K n^C,
\]
where \(F\) ranges over the arithmetic formulas defined below and
\[
\operatorname{Perm}_n(X)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\prod_{i=1}^{n}x_{i,\sigma(i)}
\in\mathbb C[x_{ij}:i,j\in[n]]?
\]
This card fixes the standard complex-field \(\mathrm{VNP}\)-versus-formula interpretation of the source’s broadly phrased explicit lower-bound challenge. By the permanent’s completeness under polynomially bounded projections, this asks whether some family in \(\mathrm{VNP}_{\mathbb C}\) lacks polynomial-size formulas; it does not impose a separate uniform construction condition on the family of small formulas being ruled out. The source’s Open Problem 8 does not itself name a field or a particular hard family, so this precise choice is an explicit editorial specification.

Superpolynomial means that no single polynomial bound works for all dimensions. It does not demand one particular exponential rate or an eventually pointwise lower bound exceeding every polynomial. There are \(n^2\) input variables; \(n\) in the displayed size bound is the matrix dimension.
why: Separating polynomial-size formulas from VNP would establish a basic limit of unrestricted algebraic expression trees for an explicit central polynomial. Formulas already allow arbitrary constants and cancellations, so their limitations are considerably harder to prove than those of many restricted algebraic models. This is a foundational lower-bound target within the hierarchy of algebraic complexity and is weaker than separating unrestricted circuits from VNP.
status_note: The 2010 survey poses the broad lower-bound challenge, and the January 2026 primary paper explicitly identifies the standard VNP-versus-unrestricted-formula separation as open. The card fixes its complex-field permanent representative and discloses that choice. The MFCS paper published on 21 August 2026 continues to discuss this general separation as a lower-bound challenge. Bounded later checks through 16 September 2026 found no verified resolution; the inspected August report claims a polynomial lower bound, while other recent results retain depth, representation or conditional restrictions. This does not independently verify all cited proofs or certify exhaustive present openness.

importance.reason: A defining unrestricted algebraic lower-bound challenge, separating the basic expression-tree model from VNP. Its reach comes from the permanent completeness theorem and the gap between known restricted-model bounds and general formulas, with consequences for the fundamental algebraic complexity hierarchy. This individually replaces the unassessed midpoint; the score reflects scope rather than recency of this review.

sentences: The question asks whether the permanent requires arithmetic expression trees larger than every fixed polynomial bound.
The trees compute formal polynomials over the complex numbers using addition and multiplication with arbitrary constants and unrestricted cancellations.
This is the explicitly selected standard separation between polynomial-size formulas and VNP, represented by the permanent through its completeness theorem.
Known bounds for restricted models and the inspected recent polynomial lower-bound claim do not establish the required unrestricted superpolynomial separation.
A complete Lean answer must rule out every polynomial formula bound or prove that one polynomial bound suffices in every dimension.

definitions:
For each integer \(n\ge1\), let \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(S_n\) be the set of all permutations of \([n]\), and let \(X=(x_{ij})_{i,j\in[n]}\) be a matrix of distinct commuting indeterminates. The permanent is the displayed sum with coefficient one on every permutation monomial. Equality of outputs is equality of formal polynomials, including all coefficients; there is no numerical input distribution, approximation error or promise on matrix entries.

An arithmetic formula is a finite rooted ordered binary tree. Each leaf is labelled by one variable \(x_{ij}\) or one constant in \(\mathbb C\); each internal vertex is labelled \(+\) or \(\times\). Its output \(\llbracket F\rrbracket\) is defined recursively by the corresponding operations in the polynomial ring. Every vertex other than the root has exactly one parent. Reusing an expression requires another copy of its subtree. A sum or product with more than two operands must be expanded into binary operations and its full tree is counted.

The size is the total number of vertices, including every occurrence of each constant and variable. Thus a leaf has size one and a binary node with subformulas \(A,B\) has size \(1+\operatorname{size}(A)+\operatorname{size}(B)\). This is one plus the edge count used by the original survey, an equivalent convention for polynomial boundedness. Arbitrary negative and nonreal constants are allowed; subtraction can be expressed using a constant \(-1\) and the permitted operations. There is no division gate, exponentiation gate, Boolean operation, test, conditional branch or determinant gate.

Constants have unit size regardless of their magnitude, algebraic degree, computability or description length. The finite tree and its constants may depend arbitrarily on \(n\); no algorithm for generating them and no finite binary encoding of arbitrary complex constants is required. A formula is a finite mathematical object with complex labels, not a bit-cost algorithm for evaluating a numerical matrix. There is no restriction on depth, cancellation, intermediate degree, repeated variables, monotonicity or homogeneity of intermediate polynomials. The output permanent is multilinear, but its subformulas need not be multilinear.

Define
\[
L_{\mathrm{perm}}(n)=\min\{\operatorname{size}(F):\llbracket F\rrbracket=\operatorname{Perm}_n\}.
\]
A finite formula exists by expanding the defining sum, so this integer minimum is well defined. The assertion is \(\forall K,C\ge1\ \exists n\ge1:\ L_{\mathrm{perm}}(n)>K n^C\). All finite initial exceptions to a prospective polynomial upper bound can be absorbed by increasing \(K\). Replacing \(n\) by the variable count \(n^2\) in the phrase polynomial size gives the same class of bounds.

For clarity, the class interpretation uses the following nonuniform algebraic definitions. A polynomial family \((f_t)_{t\ge1}\), with \(f_t\in\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_{v(t)}]\), is in \(\mathrm{VF}_{\mathbb C}\) if its variable counts, degrees and formula sizes are bounded by fixed polynomials in \(t\). It is in \(\mathrm{VNP}_{\mathbb C}\) if its variable count is polynomially bounded and there is a polynomially bounded witness count \(w(t)\) and a family \(g_t(z,y)\) of polynomial degree and polynomial-size arithmetic circuits such that
\[
f_t(z)=\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}^{w(t)}}g_t(z,b).
\]
Here a circuit uses the same inputs and binary operations as a formula, but may share intermediate results in a finite directed acyclic graph. All bounds in these class definitions use constants independent of \(t\), while circuits and constants may depend on \(t\). The zero polynomial may be assigned degree zero for these bounds. A polynomially bounded projection substitutes variables or field constants into a member of another family whose index is polynomially bounded in \(t\). The direct permanent assertion is the acceptance target; these definitions explain its class-theoretic scope without adding an algorithmic requirement.
answer_criterion:
Supply a complete, mathematically correct Lean proof of the displayed assertion or its full negation for the specified formula model.

A positive answer must prove failure of every polynomial upper bound, with the quantifier order \(\forall K,C\ \exists n\ \forall F\) in the statement. A proof for another family suffices only if its implications for this exact target are also proved. One fixed polynomial lower bound, even with a larger exponent than all currently cited bounds, does not establish the assertion.

A negative answer must prove
\[
\exists K,C\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \forall n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\
\exists F:\quad
\llbracket F\rrbracket=\operatorname{Perm}_n
\ \land\ \operatorname{size}(F)\le K n^C.
\]
The same constants work for every dimension; individual formulas and complex constants may vary with the dimension. A uniform construction is sufficient if it meets the size guarantee, but is not an additional obligation.

A lower bound only for fixed depth, monotone formulas, multilinear subformulas, bounded coefficients, or noncommuting variables does not by itself cover the formulas in this card. A polynomial-size circuit permitting shared intermediate results does not by itself provide the required formula upper bound. The numerical \(1/100\) tolerance does not change this asymptotic class-separation question.

context_blocks.text: Shpilka and Yehudayoff’s Open Problem 8 asks broadly for a superpolynomial arithmetic-formula lower bound; this card explicitly specifies the standard complex-field VNP-versus-formula version using the permanent.

The survey defines formulas as trees and proves that every VNP family over a field of characteristic different from two is a polynomially bounded projection of the permanent, supporting the chosen concrete representative.
The January 2026 Rossman–Zhu paper still identifies separating polynomial-size unrestricted formulas from VNP as a major open problem and distinguishes it from known restricted-model lower bounds.
Forbes’s 2024 result extends low-depth algebraic lower bounds to all fields, while the unrestricted depth of formulas here remains outside that guarantee.

An August 2026 report claims a permanent formula lower bound of order \(n^4/\log n\), including a version with division; this is still polynomial in the matrix dimension, and this review checks its statement rather than independently verifying its proof.
